note: INTERNAL - lists intentionally introduced weaknesses. A manifest entry is NOT evidence that the weakness exists in a running build; findings are only confirmed through recorded assessment evidence.

vulnerabilities.title: Broken object-level authorization on patient summary
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The route checks authentication and the clinical permission but skips the care-team scope check applied by GET /api/patients/:id.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A doctor can read the summary (history, allergies) of a patient who is not assigned to them; the same patient via /api/patients/:id returns 404/403.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Authenticate as doctor.mehta, enumerate patient IDs on both routes and compare.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Two responses for the same patient ID (secure route denied, lab route allowed).
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: sensitive clinical data, sequential IDs, authenticated precondition.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply canAccessPatient(user, id) in the route; add a regression test.

vulnerabilities.title: Verbose error disclosure on medication lookup
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: A malformed identifier returns the database error text, the executed statement and a stack excerpt instead of a generic message.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: GET .../medications/abc returns HTTP 500 with SQL text and stack excerpt; the secure route returns 400 with a generic message.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Send malformed IDs to both routes.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Status code and the fact (not the full text) that SQL/stack details were present.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: aids further attacks, no secrets exposed.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return a generic error with a correlation ID; log details server-side.

vulnerabilities.title: Open redirect on post-login continue link
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The redirect target is accepted when it starts with "/", which also allows protocol-relative URLs such as //other.example.test.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: next=/dashboard redirects locally; next=//other.example.test returns a 302 whose Location is an external host.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Send both values without following redirects and inspect Location.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: phishing aid, requires victim interaction.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Redirect only to server-side allow-listed paths; parse and compare origin.

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected XSS in search results page
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The q parameter is written into the HTML response without encoding and the page omits CSP and nosniff.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A harmless marker such as marker in q appears as markup in the response body.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Request with a benign HTML marker and inspect the response.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Request URL, response excerpt showing unencoded marker.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: requires victim to open crafted link; session cookie is HttpOnly.
vulnerabilities.remediation: HTML-encode output, set a restrictive CSP, avoid HTML responses from API routes.

vulnerabilities.title: User enumeration via distinct login errors
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: In vulnerable mode the login error differs for unknown users ("Unknown username") and known users ("Incorrect password").
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: Two requests with an unknown and a known username return different error text.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Compare responses for known vs unknown usernames.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: helps targeted guessing; lockout still applies.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return one generic message and equalise timing.
